movies.title: Father Of The Bride
movies.cast: Spencer Tracy, \nJoan Bennett, \nElizabeth Taylor
movies.description: Agnès Varda’s unsung feminist anthem is both a buoyant chronicle of a transformative friendship and an empowering vision of universal sisterhood. When seventeen-year-old Pauline (Valérie Mairesse) helps struggling mother of two Suzanne (Thérèse Liotard) procure the money for an abortion, a deep bond forms between the two, one that endures over the course of more than a decade as each searches for her place in the world—encountering the dawning of the women’s movement, dreamy boho musical numbers, and an Iranian adventure along the way. movies.description: Leone, Clint Eastwood, and composer Ennio Morricone’s second outing as a team finds Clint’s laconic, cold-blooded “Man with No Name” vying with fellow bounty hunter Col. Douglas Mortimer (Lee Van Cleef) to be the first to collect the price on the…

movies.title: For Sama
movies.description: Named for her daughter, For Sama depicts Waad al-Kateab’s life through five years in Aleppo. The journey takes her from economics student to her marriage to Hamza al-Kateab (later a doctor at one of Aleppo’s few remaining hospitals) and finally the birth of her daughter, all told against the backdrop of the Battle of Aleppo and succeeding conflict as it engulfs the city. She and her husband are ultimately faced with the decision to flee the city or selflessly stay in service of the war’s innocent victims.

movies.title: Freedom Way
movies.description: Freedom Way (2024) Dir. Afolabi Olalekan With Jesse Suntele, Ogranya Jable 83min; DCP Nigeria In English and Yoruba with English subtitles Software developers Themba (Jesse Suntele) and Tayo (Ogranya Jable) finally realize their long-awaited venture, Easy Go, a rideshare app connecting motorcyclists with customers across Lagos, Nigeria. The excitement of the launch quickly gives way to mounting pressure as they confront restrictive government laws, shifting regulations, and the threat of police brutality. On the periphery, the lives of nine individuals begin to collide in Afolabi Olalekan’s feature debut, a fast-paced, electric thriller shot on location in Lagos. Preceded by Ifeyinwa (2025) Dir. Jay Ikechukwu Okoroafo 13min; DCP US New York Premiere Ifeyinwa is a short film weaving director Jay Ikechukwu Okoroafo’s mother's life and migration from Enugu, Nigeria to Houston using personal family photographs, VHS footage, interviews, and sound, as told by her. The work explores the relationship between encounter, memory, and activation.

movies.title: Frontline Pbs Presents: 2000 Meters To Andriivka
movies.description: Created by FRONTLINE PBS in collaboration with the Associated Press, 2000 Meters to Andriivka offers a rare, unfiltered view of modern warfare through combat bodycam footage and intimate moments of reflection. Following a Ukrainian platoon on a high-stakes mission to liberate the village of Andriivka, the film documents not only the physical distance of 2,000 meters, but also the embedded emotional and human cost. At once visceral and deeply human, 2000 Meters to Andriivka is a stunning portrayal of war in the trenches from the Oscar-winning team behind 20 Days in Mariupol . The film is a winner of the Sundance Film Festival’s World Cinema Documentary Directing Award, the Directors Guild of America Award for Outstanding Directorial Achievement in Documentary, the Writers Guild of America Award for Best Documentary Screenplay, and the American Society of Cinematographers Award, and has been nominated for Emmy and Peabody Awards. Join us for a post-screening conversation with special guests connected to the film. Created by BAM and FRONTLINE PBS Impact teams, this program is rooted in a shared mission to spark dialogue, deepen cultural understanding, and engage audiences around meaningful social issues.

movies.title: Gabbeh
movies.description: Mohsen Makhmalbaf journeyed to Iran’s remote steppes to film a vanishing nomadic tribe, but, enchanted by the landscape and the stories woven into their gabbeh carpets, his documentary evolved into a lyrical folktale. On a riverbank, an elderly couple washes their gabbeh . From its woven threads emerges a beautiful young woman—Gabbeh herself—who tells her story: She loves a mysterious horseman who trails her nomadic clan across the mountains. Though her father has blessed their union, seasons pass and the rider only circles closer, never arriving. This tender romance is interlaced with the lives of the nomads, whose days are shaped by nature’s rhythms and the brilliantly-hued carpets that hold their histories.

movies.title: Gail Daughtry And The Celebrity Sex Pass
movies.cast: Zoey Deutch, Jon Hamm, John Slattery, Ken Marino, Miles Gutierrez-Riley, Ben Wang, Joe Lo Truglio, and Sabrina Impacciatore
movies.description: Small town hairdresser Gail Daughtry is engaged to her devoted high school sweetheart, Tom. Her life takes a turn when a trip to a book signing leads to Tom meeting – and sleeping – with his “celebrity pass”. Reeling from the betrayal, Gail impulsively joins her friend Otto on a trip to Los Angeles, where a psychic convinces Gail that the only way to save her marriage is to “even the scales” with her own celebrity pass: Jon Hamm. Thus begins an epic journey through Tinseltown as Gail and Otto join forces with a talent agency assistant, a paparazzo, and actor John Slattery, all in the search for Hamm. Along the way, they collide with celebrities and are hunted by a group of Italian assassins as they get ever closer to finding the elusive star.

movies.title: Gaza Fights For Freedom
movies.description: In this gut-wrenching depiction of Gaza’s protest movement, Abby Martin paints a portrait of a people determined to return to their historic homeland. This film features a plethora of interviews with Palestinians participating in the Great March of Return, a weekly series of protests that saw tens of thousands march up to the border fence between Gaza and Israel. While hundreds were killed and thousands were injured, these protests continued unabated for months. Amid tragedy, Martin encounters immense hope and steadfastness, proving that a people can only remain oppressed for so long.

movies.title: Germaine Acogny - The Essence Of Dance
movies.description: North American Premiere Germaine Acogny, the "mother of African contemporary dance," is one of Africa’s most influential artists. This documentary traces her journey as a pioneer in blending traditional West African dance with European influences, creating the Acogny Technique, which has shaped contemporary dance worldwide. With over 50 years of performing and teaching, the 80-year-old dance icon received the Golden Lion for Dance at the 2021 Venice Dance Festival for her lifetime achievements. Followed by a Q&A with Ghyslaine de Souza, Germaine Acogny’s daughter, moderated by Tracy Austin

movies.title: Girls Like Girls
movies.cast: Maya da Costa, Myra Molloy, Zach Braff
movies.description: Based on Hayley Kiyoko’s breakthrough hit song and viral music video of the same name, the film tells the universal story of falling in love for the first time and learning to accept yourself along the way.

movies.title: Girls Like Girls
movies.cast: Maya da Costa, Myra Molloy, Zach Braff
movies.description: Based on writer/director Hayley Kiyoko's hit single and best-selling novel of the same name and featuring all-new music from Kiyoko, GIRLS LIKE GIRLS is a heartfelt coming-of-age story set over the course of one sun-drenched summer, where new-girl-in-town Coley falls in love for the first time while learning to accept herself along the way.

movies.title: Godzilla vs. Biollante
movies.description:
Presented in Japanese with English subtitles
Following the events of RETURN OF GODZILLA, genetic scientists, the Japanese government, and terrorists collide over the ownership of Godzilla’s DNA. Following an act of industrial sabotage, Dr. Shiragami fuses both Godzilla’s and his daughter’s cells with plant information and inadvertently creates the biological terror Biollante.
A parable over a sustainable future set against chaotic uncertainty, GODZILLA VS. BIOLLANTE doubles down on the explosive effects from its predecessor to deliver another high-stakes monster mash.

movies.title: Golden Goal Presents: Offside
movies.description: In Tehran, a girl (Shima Mobarak-Shahi) disguises her gender to elude the regime’s stadium ban against women ahead of a men’s qualifying match for the 2006 World Cup. When she is detained and jailed, she joins a group of riotous women bent on watching their country play. Bored but dutiful soldiers look after the women, and occasionally provide game commentary. Bold Iranian cinema luminary Jafar Panahi ( It Was Just an Accident , No Bears ) was inspired by his own football-loving daughter’s exploits to make Offside , filming at the actual match with two improvised outcomes prepared to anticipate victory or defeat. Golden Goal , an independent literary magazine, explores the politics and allure of the World Cup. Celebrating this year’s series, BAM is thrilled to screen Offside , followed by a discussion with Iranian author Amir Ahmadi Arian and Solmaz Sharif, founder of Shirzanan , the first women’s sports magazine in Iran, moderated by Golden Goal co-editors Miguel Salazar and Alex Shephard.

movies.title: Gonza The Spearman
movies.description: New 4K Restoration “Gonza the Spearman is a tragic period drama based on a classic play by Chikamatsu Monzaemon. The story follows Gonza, a low-ranking samurai whose life unravels after he becomes caught in a forbidden relationship with his lord’s wife. Bound by rigid social codes and ideas of honor, the pair are pushed toward an inevitable tragedy. With elegant cinematography, restrained pacing, and strong influences from traditional bunraku puppet theater, the film creates a tense, emotionally rich atmosphere, anchored by a subtle performance from Ken Ogata.” - Shun Inoue

movies.title: Good Time
movies.description: A relentless, breakneck, candy-colored chase through the heart of Queens and Nassau County, the Safdies’ long, dark night of the soul thriller follows ne’er-do-well punk grifter “Connie” Nikas (Robert Pattinson) as he scrambles to spring brother…

movies.title: Good Time
movies.description: A precursor to Uncut Gems and Marty Supreme , the Safdie Brothers’ heart-pumping style of snowballing, stake-raising antics was solidified with Good Time . After a botched bank robbery lands his younger brother in prison, Constantine "Connie" Nikas (Robert Pattinson) embarks on a twisted odyssey through the city's underworld in an increasingly desperate—and dangerous—attempt to get his brother Nick (Benny Safdie) out of jail. Over the course of one adrenalized night, Connie finds himself on a mad descent into violence and mayhem as he races against the clock to save his brother and himself, knowing their lives hang in the balance.

movies.title: Goodbye, Dragon Inn
movies.description: Like the Royal Theater in The Last Picture Show and the movie house in Cinema Paradiso , the Fu-Ho, a run down Taipei movie palace, is shutting down for good, playing its final film to a motley smattering of spectators. Even as the theater's ill-mannered patrons snack noisily, remove their shoes, and generally treat this temple of cinema like their living room, the sense that moviegoing as a communal experience is slipping away takes on a powerful and painful resonance. Yet Tsai Ming-liang’s Goodbye, Dragon Inn is too multifaceted to collapse into a simple valentine to the age of pre-VOD cinephilia. Instead, Ming-liang rises to the narrative challenge, offering a series of sly and delicate character arcs via his signature long, static shots and sparse use of dialogue. Featuring a reading by James Malzone before the screening on February 19

movies.title: Greetings From Out Here
movies.description: Accompanied by her dog Sam and a video camera, filmmaker Ellen Spiro traveled from Virginia to Texas and back exploring openly gay culture in the Deep South. Highlighted by spontaneous encounters with local eccentrics and mechanics (her van breaks down frequently), Greetings from Out Here provides detailed portraits of small-town queer Southerners—from Rita, a retired military officer turned drag queen in New Orleans to Iris, a Black lesbian living in a bus in the Ozarks. Filmed on location at the Texas Gay Rodeo, Mardi Gras, Gay Pride in Atlanta, Dollywood, Miss Miller's Eternal Love and Care Pet Cemetery, and the Short Mountain Radical Faerie sanctuary, Spiro captures the richness, vitality and courage of "out" gay Southern life in the early 1990s.

movies.title: Guillermo del Toro's Pinocchio
movies.description: During the rise of fascism in Mussolini's Italy, a wooden boy brought magically to life struggles to live up to his father's expectations.

movies.title: Güeros
movies.description: Ever since the National University strike broke out, Sombra (Huerta) and Santos (Ortizgris) have been living in angst-ridden limbo. Education-less, motionless, purposeless, and unsure of what the strike will bring, they begin to look for strange ways to kill time. But their idiosyncratic routine is interrupted by the unexpected arrival of Tomas (Aguirre), Sombra's kid brother. Unable to fit in amongst these older slackers, Tomas discovers that unsung Mexican folk-rock hero Epigmenio Cruz has been hospitalized somewhere in the city. Tomas convinces Sombra and Santos they must track him down in order to pay their final respects on his deathbed. But what they thought would be a simple trip to find their childhood idol soon becomes a voyage of self-discovery across Mexico City's invisible frontiers.

movies.title: Haifa
movies.description: Haifa, nicknamed after the city he longs for, comes and goes in a Palestinian refugee camp. Although he is seen as the town fool, there are many things that only he knows. He is closely related to the family of Abu Said, a former policeman who has high hopes for the political developments promised by the peace process. Oum Said, his wife, hangs her hope instead on the imminent release of their eldest son, Said, from jail. Their youngest son, Siad, is cynical and rebellious. Sabah, their 12-year-old daughter, sees the future through the eyes of a romantic, searching for what it might hold in store for her.

movies.title: Hamnet
movies.description: In 16th-century England, an impoverished Latin tutor named William Shakespeare (Mescal) meets free-spirited Agnes (Buckley), sparking an affair that leads to marriage and three children. As Will seeks his fortune in the London theater, Agnes anchors the domestic sphere alone. The couple’s bond is tested when tragedy strikes, but their shared experience sets the stage for the creation of Shakespeare’s timeless masterpiece, Hamlet . Academy Award-winning filmmaker Chloé Zhao ( Nomadland , The Rider ) illuminates the complexities of love and the healing power of art and creativity.

movies.title: Himiko
movies.description: 35mm print imported from Japan (courtesy National Film Archive of Japan) Drawing again from the forms of Japanese theater and visual arts, this singular film retells the story of Himiko: a shaman queen in ancient Japan who is central to Shinto and national origin stories. Using the past to comment on the present, Shinoda presents Himiko navigating the patriarchal military powers of the surrounding kingdoms as well as her own physical desire for her recently returned half-brother. With a brilliant performance by Shima Iwashita—an actress in the work of Ozu, Kinoshita, and Kobayashi, as well as Shinoda’s wife and long time collaborator— Himiko was made in collaboration with the legendary avant garde Japanese film production company Art Theater Guild.

movies.title: How To Build A Library
movies.description: In 2017, Kenyan writer Shiro Koinange and publisher Angela Wachuka set out to reclaim Nairobi’s McMillan Memorial Library, a colonial-era institution that had once barred Black patrons and remained frozen in the image of the British Empire. Determined to transform the decaying monument into a vibrant public space, they secure a tenuous management contract, inherit a skeptical staff, and begin reimagining its collections, programming, and purpose. As they digitize hundreds of thousands of texts and challenge colonial knowledge systems embedded in structures like the Dewey Decimal classification, tensions arise—both internally and externally with government officials whose shifting demands threaten the project’s future. Fundraising galas, satellite library launches, and even a visit from King Charles III bring visibility and prestige, yet underscore the enduring entanglements of colonial history and contemporary power. Despite political instability and bureaucratic uncertainty, Shiro and Wachuka’s efforts ultimately transform the once-exclusionary library into a dynamic cultural hub, embodying a broader struggle to redefine Kenya’s past and imagine its sovereign future. Followed by a Q&A with Damilola Lemomu (June Givanni Archives) and Angela Wachuka, moderated by Daniella Brito

movies.title: I Am Black, I Am Beautiful
movies.description: I Am Black, I Am Beautiful (2023) Dir. Sabrina Onana 83min; DCP France New York Premiere Twelve Afro-French women talk about their relationship with hair, beauty standards, men, and representation in the media. Their journey of doubts, growth, alienation, reconciliation, resilience, and self-acceptance raises awareness about social and cultural issues in both African and Western societies. By publicly sharing their experiences, the documentary creates space for these women to speak, be seen, and be heard, while fostering an honest dialogue both within and beyond the Black community. Followed by a Q&A with director Sabrina Onana, moderated by Felicia Appenteng Preceded by: Children of Diaspora (2024) Dir. Sabrina Onana With Edwina Adelard, Mansour Diop, Monika Néréa Mouanza 8min; DCP France In French with English subtitles Through the inner monologue of a child of African immigrants, the film brings us originally and poetically to the heart of the identity journey of diaspora children.

movies.title: I Love Boosters
movies.description: In another surreal, politically-charged, and straight-up weird outing from eccentric director Boots Riley ( Sorry to Bother You ), I Love Boosters follows a crew of professional shoplifters (Keke Palmer, Naomi Ackie) as they take aim at a cutthroat fashion maven (Demi Moore)—in an effort they deem a community service. Sneak preview screening on May 19 at 7:30pm followed by a Q&A with Boots Riley

movies.title: I Shot Andy Warhol
movies.cast: Lili Taylor, Jared Harris, Martha Plimpton, Stephen Dorff
movies.description: The scintillating feature debut of Mary Harron (AMERICAN PSYCHO) and one of the most controversial independent films of the 1990s, I SHOT ANDY WARHOL stars an electric Lili Taylor as Valerie Solanas, a militant feminist whose attempted murder of Andy Warhol brought instant fame to her radically anti-male SCUM Manifesto. Dropping out of grad school in the mid '60s, the brilliant yet volatile Solanas survived in New York City as a destitute artist, sex worker, and panhandler, soon striking up a friendship with Warhol superstar Candy Darling that brought her briefly into the orbit of the world’s premier pop artist. With vivid, hallucinatory attention to historical detail, Harron captures the explosive cross-pollination of New York’s political and artistic countercultures, as well as the creativity, snobbery, and decadence at the heart of the legendary Factory. Anchored by pitch-perfect performances – and featuring a blistering score by John Cale as well as covers of '60s hits by some of the '90s' most iconic bands (R.E.M., Wilco) – I SHOT ANDY WARHOL is an incisive portrait of a rebel without an outlet and the soon-to-be-lost generation she came to define. (Janus)

movies.title: Igualada + Landslide (Avalancha)
movies.description: Landslide (Avalancha) (2023) Dir. Daniel Santiago Cortés Ramírez 25min; DCP In Spanish with English subtitles Composed entirely of archival footage, this experimental documentary opens with solely sound: scraping, rattling, and rumbling, like pebbles coming loose and starting to roll down a slope. The earth stirs before it starts to slide. What follows is a procession that runs through time and always takes a different form. A funeral procession, a protest march, a sea of fedoras, uniformed men on horses. And the sound continues to swell. The result is not just a depiction of Colombian history, but of resistance broadly, and the lives lost in its wake. Igualada (2024) Dir. Juan Mejia Botero 81min; DCP In Spanish with English subtitles Deemed “rousing and intimate” by Variety , Botero’s film follows the 2022 campaign of Francia Márquez, a Black woman from a rural background in her pursuit of Colombia’s presidency. The film’s title, defined by an opening caption as “a derogatory term (based on class, race and gender) used to designate someone who acts as if they deserve rights and privileges that supposedly don’t correspond to them,” is transformed through Márquez’s campaign, drawing the historically underrepresented into the nation’s political process. Filmed over the course of 15 years, Botero provides a portrait that is both personal and socially moving.

movies.title: Inherent Vice
movies.description: The second Paul Thomas Anderson adaptation of a Pynchon novel ( The Master was loosely inspired by V) follows Larry "Doc" Sportello (Phoenix), a bungling private investigator fumbling through the criminal underworld of 1970 Los Angeles. Arguably the most quintessential presentation of Pynchon put to film tonally, the narration—as read by the musician Joanna Newsom—pulls some of the novel’s text verbatim.

movies.title: Inventing Cinema: Moustapha Alassane + Georges Mélies
movies.description: The invention of cinema was not a singular moment, but a series of parallel discoveries across the globe. Honoring the national film cultures of Niger and France, Inventing Cinema reintroduces the medium through two of its pioneering magicians. During the moving image’s nascent period, Georges Méliès bridged the nineteenth and twentieth centuries with fantastical experiments of theatricality and spectacle. Drawing on his background as an actor and illusionist, the French filmmaker invented editing techniques that continue to inform modern movie creation. Decades later, the autodidact Alassane Moustapha’s precocious childhood puppet shows and shadow plays laid the foundation for an improvised reinvention of cinema. Moustapha made films before ever seeing a camera, but eventually received formal training that led to a wayward and whimsical filmography of trenchant political satires, animated fables, and imaginative transpositions of oral storytelling. movies.title: Is This Thing On?
movies.description: As their marriage quietly unravels, Alex (Arnett) faces middle age and an impending divorce, seeking new purpose in the New York comedy scene while Tess (Dern) confronts the sacrifices she made for their family—forcing them to navigate co-parenting, identity, and whether love can take a new form. Bradley Cooper writes, directs, and co-stars in this understated, affecting portrait of the challenges and opportunities of starting over in middle age.

movies.title: Jack Johnson: Surfilmusic
movies.cast: Jack Johnson
movies.description: A positive, warm and intimate look into Jack Johnson’s evolution from surfer to filmmaker to world-renowned musician. The documentary traces how his early years making surf films with close friends became a foundation for a much broader creative life, capturing moments in and out of the water that later surfaced in his songwriting. Blending rare footage from those formative surf films and Johnson's personal and family archives with present-day reflections, the film weaves together how lived experience, friendship, and exploration shaped the sound and stories behind the music. Featuring Jack Johnson, Kelly Slater, Rob Machado, Gerry Lopez, Chris Malloy, G Love, Ben Harper, John Florence, Tamayo Perry, Emmett Malloy, Kim Johnson, and more.

movies.title: Jackass: Best and Last
movies.description: A joyously raucous celebration of all the mischievous camaraderie that you’ve come to love and expect from these idiots

movies.title: jackass: best and last
movies.description:
If just hearing the words "Hi, I'm Johnny Knoxville" fires up the pleasure centers of your brain, then JACKASS: BEST AND LAST is the movie event you've been training for your entire life. For 25 years, Knoxville, Steve-O, Wee Man, Chris Pontius, and a rotating cast of willing idiots have dedicated themselves to answering one question: "What if we did something incredibly dangerous, incredibly dumb, and filmed it?" The result is one of the funniest, most painful, and most unexpectedly heartwarming franchises ever created.
Now the gang is back for one final ride. JACKASS: BEST AND LAST combines brand-new stunts with the most legendary moments from the series' gloriously reckless history. So gather your buddies, order a drink, and join us for one last victory lap with the patron saints of poor impulse control.

movies.title: JACKIE THE STRIPPER
movies.description: Set in London's Whitechapel district in 1888, Jackie/Lottie finds herself plagued by the infamous Jack The Ripper who is head of a secret organization known only as The Court. Only one man, John Grey, stands up to the Ripper, vowing to fight against the tryanny, carnage and male oppression that is left in the court's wake. Cut to modern day, and a group of kick-ass female assassins, led by their leader Jackie, plan a series of hits that will leave The Court dead in their tracks. movies.title: Jeanne Dielman, 23 Quai Du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles
movies.description: A singular and uniquely influential moment in film history, Chantal Akerman’s Jeanne Dielman, 23, quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles meticulously details, with a sense of impending doom, the daily routine of a middle-aged widow. In its enormous spareness, Akerman’s film seems simple, but it encompasses an entire world. Both an exacting character study and one of cinema’s most hypnotic and complete depictions of space and time, the slice-of-life narrative, composed of long takes and lingering sequences, ranked first in 2022’s Sight and Sound critic’s poll of the greatest films of all time.

movies.title: Julia
movies.description: Based on a chapter from Lillian Hellman's 1973 autobiographical work Pentimento , Zinnemann’s political drama traces the stories of two women and the intersections of their lives before and during the Nazi era. The film, a tribute to a memory of Hellman’s childhood friend Julia (Redgrave), recounts the occasion of Julia’s request that Hellmen herself (Fonda) undertake a dangerous mission in service of the fight against Naziism.

movies.title: Klute
movies.description: In the first installment of what would eventually come to be referred to as Pakula’s "paranoia trilogy" (followed by The Parallax View and All the President's Men ), Fonda hauntingly portrays Bree Daniels, a high-priced call girl stalked by a psychopath. When she crosses paths with private eye John Klute (Sutherland), a blossoming romance thrusts Klute into the position of protector as he unravels the extent of Daniels’ predicament. Fonda won the Academy Award for Best Actress for her tour-de-force performance, cementing the eerie tone of a film that investigates surveillance and the weight of being watched.

movies.title: L'Age D'Or (With Un Chien Andalou)
movies.cast: Gaston Modot, Lya Lys
movies.description: Agnès Varda’s unsung feminist anthem is both a buoyant chronicle of a transformative friendship and an empowering vision of universal sisterhood. When seventeen-year-old Pauline (Valérie Mairesse) helps struggling mother of two Suzanne (Thérèse Liotard) procure the money for an abortion, a deep bond forms between the two, one that endures over the course of more than a decade as each searches for her place in the world—encountering the dawning of the women’s movement, dreamy boho musical numbers, and an Iranian adventure along the way. Initially divisive for its sunny, idealized view of female liberation, ONE SINGS, THE OTHER DOESN'T now seems all the more radical—and all the more vital—for its unabashedly utopian spirit.

movies.title: La Collectionneuse
movies.description: The third entry in Rohmer’s Six Moral Tales series, in which cinematographer Néstor Almendros takes magnificent advantage of the glorious natural light of the French Riviera, is a deceptively lovely film about less-than-lovely behavior, an ironic study…

movies.title: La Haine
movies.description: A cinematic Molotov cocktail that was the first onscreen description of life (and death) in Paris’s banlieue housing projects that many French filmgoers had ever seen, La Haine depicts three armed and angry slum kids—Vincent Cassel, Hubert Koundé,…

movies.title: Lady
movies.description: In the restless night of Lagos, one of the city’s few female cab drivers, Lady, survives by staying tough and focused. She dreams of escape, saving her earnings for a new life far from the chaos of this Nigerian metropolis. But when long-lost childhood friend, Pinky - now a sex worker - returns with a burst of colour and trouble, Lady is pulled reluctantly into her orbit. Soon she’s driving a crew of glamorous, reckless, fun-loving women through the underbelly of Lagos nightlife. What begins as judgement becomes unexpected sisterhood: wild, tender, and disarming. As Lady becomes entangled in their world the nights grow more dangerous, and the city presses harder against old wounds she’s never confronted. Forced to face the trauma she’s long outrun, she cracks open - learning to feel, to belong, to see herself through new eyes. When everything reaches breaking point, Lady must make a choice that will change her life’s direction forever. In that choice lies a new kind of freedom: one rooted not in escape, but in transformation. Followed by a Q&A with director Olive Nwosu, moderated by Karen McMullen

movies.title: Laila’S Birthday
movies.description: When government cuts force a judge (Mohammed Bakri) to make a career pivot, Abu Laila finds himself driving a taxi in the hectic streets of the West Bank. On the day of his daughter's birthday, his wife insists that he needs to be home early with a present and a cake. The proud ex-judge embarks on a sprawling urban odyssey plagued by gridlock, disorderly passengers, and the myriad plights affecting daily life under occupation.

movies.title: Last Year at Marienbad
movies.description: Variously pilloried and adulated in its time, and undeniably “one of the most influential movies ever made” [J. Hoberman, The Village Voice], Resnais’s coolly glittering, fascinating, frustrating film, made in collaboration with novelist Alain…

movies.title: Last Year At Marienbad
movies.description: Not just a defining work of the French New Wave but one of the great, lasting mysteries of modern art, Alain Resnais’s epochal Last Year at Marienbad (L ’année dernière à Marienbad ) has puzzled appreciative viewers for decades. Written by Alain Robbe-Grillet, a radical master of the New Novel, this surreal fever dream gorgeously fuses timelines while telling the ambiguous tale of a man and a woman (Giorgio Albertazzi and Delphine Seyrig) who may or may not have met a year ago, perhaps at the very same cathedral-like, mirror-filled château they now find themselves wandering. Unforgettable in both its haunting scope and confounding details (gilded ceilings, diabolical parlor games, a loaded gun, sudden appearances and disappearances) Resnais’s investigation into the nature of memory is disturbing, romantic, and maybe even a ghost story.

movies.title: Late Spring
movies.description: Widowed father Shukichi (Chishû Ryû) and his dotingly devoted 27-year-old daughter Noriko (Setsuko Hara) have through the years settled into a comfortable routine of domestic harmony—that is, until Noriko’s aunt (Haruko Sugimura) convinces Shukichi…

movies.title: Le Pont Du Nord
movies.description: A bank robber (Bulle Ogier) recently released from prison and a young woman (portrayed by Bulle’s daughter, Pascale) roam the streets of Paris, cinematically reimagined as a sprawling board game, in a quest to understand the contents of a mysterious suitcase. A gorgeously rendered portrait of Paris imbued with an ever-present ominous rhythm, the playful middle period work from Rivette shares with Pynchon an interest in conspiracy and secret histories.

movies.title: Lebanon in Turmoil preceded by South Lebanon
movies.description: Saab had aspired to attend film school in her youth, but eventually found her way into cinema via journalism. Her first nonfiction feature, begun shortly after the slaughter of some six thousand Palestinians by right-wing Christian Phalangists in April…

movies.title: Leviticus
movies.cast: Joe Bird, Stacy Clausen
movies.description: Two teenage boys must escape a violent entity that takes the form of the person they desire most - each other

movies.title: Leviticus
movies.cast: Joe Bird, Stacy Clausen
movies.description: In a conservative Australian town, the most terrifying thing facing two queer teens isn’t just the ostracization of their community, but a more sinister entity that takes the form of the person they desire most: each other. With captivating performances from its breakout stars, this striking debut from director Adrian Chiarella deftly weaves a truly haunting premise and moments of sweet romance into a larger tapestry investigating the toll of contemporary bigotry.

movies.title: Leviticus
movies.cast: Joe Bird, Stacy Clausen
movies.description: In the latest horror from the producers of TALK TO ME and THE BABADOOK, two teenage boys must escape a violent entity that takes the form of the person they desire most – each other. Doppelgängers, conversion camp, and a shape-shifting monster make for a movie that crawls under your skin and stays there. Don’t miss it in theaters.

movies.title: Light of Day
movies.description: Bruce Springsteen was originally intended to star in Schrader’s blue-collar rock ’n’ roll melodrama, but after the Boss took off with its original title in his back pocket—“Born in the U.S.A.”—he presented the renamed Light of Day as a title…

movies.title: Los Angeles Plays Itself
movies.description: Los Angeles is more than where movies are made; it also provides the thematic undercurrent for a myriad of iconic moments in cinema history. Thom Andersen's documentary Los Angeles Plays Itself explores this complicated tapestry and the ways in which the town and the works created within it interact. An avowed fan of classic Hollywood, the west coast mecca has a major place in Pynchon’s personal lore as his primary residence in the 60s and early 70s. His examination of the city’s counter culture up close in Manhattan Beach informs a lot of his west coast novels, which are comfortably in conversation with Thom Anderson’s magnum opus on Hollywood and the history of power in California.

movies.title: Los Nadie (The Nobodies)
movies.description: In Medellín, five friends on the precipice of leaving adolescence are entrenched in the unrest, rage, and tenderness of youth. Living on the outskirts of a city that excludes them, they embrace music, street art, and friendship as weapons of resistance in this coming of age ensemble film.

movies.title: Los Olvidados (The Young And The Damned)
movies.cast:
Stella Inda, 
Miguel Inclán, 
Alfonso Mejía, 
Roberto Cobo
movies.description: Made during Luis Buñuel’s prolific two-decade period in Mexico, Los olvidados won the country’s second major prize at Cannes, following the landmark win of María Candelaria (1944). This against-formula juvenile crime drama showcases the power of Indigenous actress Estela Inda, recipient of a Silver Ariel for Best Supporting Actress for her memorable performance as the mother of the film’s young, impressionable protagonist; both characters try their damnedest to rise above the crime festering in the slums of Mexico City.

movies.title: Los Punks + Beyond The Screams
movies.description: From Los Angeles to Chicago, New York, Santa Fe, and more, the Latino/Chicano punk movement developed within the U.S. as a means for young people to express themselves and resist growing societal oppression. Los Punks showcases the development of this movement specifically in LA, while Beyond the Screams explores the wider development of Latino punk throughout the U.S. from the ‘70s through the early ‘90s. Los Punks: We Are All We Have (2016) Dir. Angela Boatwright 79min; Digital This intimate documentary follows teens and young adults who find meaning in the thriving punk rock scene in the backyards of South Central and East Los Angeles. Beyond the Screams (Mas Alla de Los Gritos) (1999) Dir. Martin Sorondeguy 29min; Digital In English and Spanish with English subtitles From the late 1970s up until the early 1990s, young people looking for a way to empower themselves began to develop a Latino/Chicano punk movement across the U.S. Martin Sorrondeguy, singer of hardcore punk bands Los Crudos and Limp Wrist, and a prominent figure in both the straight edge scene and the queercore scene, follows the development of the scene through the decades in major Latino cities. Composed of interviews and live performances, this film focuses on the struggle of Latino/Chicano artists against globalization, poverty, and identity.

movies.title: Lost Highway
movies.cast: Bill Pullman, Patricia Arquette, John Roselius, Balthazar Getty
movies.description: From this inventory of imagery, Lynch fashions two separate but intersecting stories, one about a jazz musician (Bill Pullman), tortured by the notion that his wife is having an affair, who suddenly finds himself accused of her murder. The other is a young mechanic (Balthazar Getty) drawn into a web of deceit by a temptress who is cheating on her gangster boyfriend. These two tales are linked by the fact that the women in both are played by the same actress (Patricia Arquette).

movies.title: Love in the Afternoon
movies.description: The capstone entry of Rohmer’s Moral Tales series stars Bernard Verley as a happily married lawyer who assures us via voiceover that his wandering eye is in fact proof positive of his unshakable fidelity—but then his serene rectitude is tested sorely…

movies.title: Love Letter
movies.description: Q&A with director Shunji Iwai on Friday, June 5th and Introduction by director Shunji Iwai on Saturday, June 6th

movies.title: Maddie's Secret
movies.cast: John Early, Kate Berlant, Eric Rahill, Kristen Johnston, Claudia O'Doherty, Conner O'Malley, Vanessa Bayer, Chris Bauer
movies.description: MADDIE’S SECRET is comedian, writer, and actor John Early’s critically acclaimed directorial debut starring himself as Maddie, a plucky dishwasher who leaps to viral superstardom at a trendy food content creation company. While her life seems picturesque – complete with an adoring husband (Eric Rahill), ride-or-die best friend (Kate Berlant), and a cupboard full of woman-owned, ethically-sourced chili crisp to boot – mounting professional pressures threaten to reawaken a hidden secret from her troubled past. A pitch-perfect blend of satire, melodrama, daring tonal shifts, and intimate performances, the film marks a bold new voice in contemporary cinema.

movies.cast: John Early, Kate Berlant, Eric Rahill, Kristen Johnston, Claudia O'Doherty, Conner O'Malley, Vanessa Bayer, Chris Bauer

movies.title: Made in Hong Kong
movies.description: The first independent film released in post-Handover Hong Kong, Chan’s atmospheric shoestring-budget character study is a rough-and-ready piece of work shot on grainy leftover 35mm short ends in the city’s overcrowded subsidized housing projects. The…

movies.title: Maid in Manhattan
movies.description: Outer-borough striver marries up. Part of the series Locations, Locations, Locations . On June 28, the 6pm screening will be followed by a Q&A with location manager Lyn Pinezich, who will also introduce the 8:15pm screening.

movies.title: Malcolm X
movies.description: The culmination of a longtime dream, Malcolm X exemplifies director Spike Lee’s unique vision and style, moving elegantly between genres and time periods with a dazzling array of camera movements and meticulous editing as he tells the life story of the iconic leader. Denzel Washington embodies Malcolm with conviction, force, and dignity in one of his most indelible performances.

movies.title: Maluala
movies.description: Maluala takes us into a palenque —a fortified settlement of escaped slaves—hidden in Cuba’s eastern mountains, as the Spanish colonial forces attempt to sow discord among their leaders. The film marks Giral’s third entry into his trilogy of films about slavery in 19th-century Cuba and the Caribbean, combining a Marxist lens with the long arc of Black Liberation to trace the development from individual to collective struggle.

movies.title: Mamma Mia!
movies.cast:
Meryl Streep, 
Pierce Brosnan, 
Colin Firth, 
Stellan Skarsgård, 
Julie Walters, 
Dominic Cooper, 
Amanda Seyfried,

movies.description: Introduction by actor John "Lypsinka" Epperson on Saturday, June 13th

movies.title: Marty Supreme
movies.description: Timothée Chalamet “makes one of the most colossal movie performances of the 21st century seem as natural as a lay-up” ( IndieWire ) in the latest offering from director Josh Safdie (co-director, Good Time , Uncut Gems ). Performing with a distinguished cast that includes Gwyneth Paltrow, Odessa A'zion, and Tyler Okonma (a.k.a. Tyler, the Creator), Chalamet gives “the defining performance of his still-burgeoning career” ( Variety ) as would-be ping-pong champion Marty Mauser, a young man with a dream no one respects, who goes to hell and back in pursuit of greatness.

movies.title: Mary Jane'S Not A Virgin Anymore
movies.description: When a bright, self-possessed movie theater employee decides to lose her virginity, she discovers that sex is less a rite of passage than a series of awkward negotiations. Sasha Jacobson’s ( I Was a Teenage Serial Killer ) sharply observed indie coming-of-age story charts the debauched misadventures of a slacker squad of co-workers. Keep an eye out for cameos by iconic punk frontmen Jello Biafra and Davey Havok. Featuring a reading by Josh Bayer before the screening on February 14.

movies.title: María Antonia
movies.description: New York Premiere of New Restoration This tragedy follows a rebellious woman living in an Afro-Cuban Havana neighborhood during the 1950s, and the crime of passion that arises amid her entangled love life. Followed by a Q&A with writer Armando Dorrego

movies.title: Master And Commander: The Far Side Of The World
movies.description: In this saga set during the Napoleonic Wars, adapted loosely from Patrick O'Brian's Aubrey–Maturin series, a captain of the British Royal Navy (Crowe) pursues his enemy across the seas—posing questions about the interplay between duty and loyalty along the way. The Pynchon connection? The novelist names a storyteller—“the best Yarn-Spinner in all the Fleets”—after O’Brian in Mason & Dixon , his own sprawling historical adventure tale.

movies.title: Masters of the Universe (2026)
movies.description: Director Travis Knight brings the legendary franchise back to the big screen in this epic live-action adventure. After being separated for 15 years, the Sword of Power leads Prince Adam (Nicholas Galitzine) back to Eternia, where he discovers his home shattered under the fiendish rule of Skeletor (Jared Leto). To save his family and his world, Adam must join forces with his closest allies, Teela (Camila Mendes) and Duncan/Man-At-Arms (Idris Elba), and embrace his true destiny as He-Man – the most powerful man in the universe.

movies.title: MATADOR BOLERO
movies.description: A New York nightclub becomes the site of a high-profile murder that attracts the attention of an obsessive detective, a TV news reporter, and an elusive being living outside the realms of time and space. Youtube linkhere Tickets:https://www.eventbrite.com/e/matador-bolero-tickets-1992292218657?aff=oddtdtcreator

movies.title: May Your Eyes Be Blessed: Film And Tv Work Of Luiz Fernando Carvalho
movies.description: Programmed by Madeleine Molyneaux & Carlos Valladares Luiz Fernando Carvalho is among the most inventive visual stylists in Brazilian film and television, yet his poetic, unruly oeuvre remains largely unknown in the US. Inspired by the examples of Glauber Rocha, Marguerite Duras, Pier Paolo Pasolini, and Luchino Visconti, Carvalho has brought a bold, “contaminated” sensibility to feverish adaptations of texts by Machado de Assis, Ariano Suassuna, Graciliano Ramos, and especially Clarice Lispector, while also reinterpreting Brazil’s history, myths, and emotional and political landscapes. This series includes the North American premiere of The Passion According to G.H. , Carvalho’s award-winning treatment of Lispector’s supposedly “unfilmable” 1964 novel, plus his landmark first feature film, To the Left of the Father (Lavoura Arcaica) , and more celebrated work in cinema and television. Also screening are films personally selected by Carvalho that have fired his imagination. This overdue retrospective introduces New York audiences to a filmmaker hailed by Bernardo Bertolucci as “master of himself and of us all.” Luiz Fernando Carvalho and actress Maria Fernanda Cândido will be present for select events.

movies.title: Meantime
movies.description: Produced for Britain’s Channel 4, Leigh’s bleakly comic drama shuttles between the Pollocks, a working-class East End family headed by working mum Mavis (Pam Ferris) and on-the-dole dad Frank (Jeff Robert), barely scraping by from day to day, and…

movies.title: Memories Of Love Returned
movies.description: On April 24, 2002, filmmaker Ntare Guma Mbaho Mwine’s car broke down in the small town of Mbirizi, Uganda. While waiting for it to be repaired, he stumbled upon a small photo studio and met photographer Kibaate Aloysius Ssalongo, whose work spanned from the late 1950s to his death in 2006. This chance encounter turned into a 22-year journey documenting and exploring Kibaate’s life, photography, and the profound impact his work had on the community he documented, as well as Mwine’s own life. Followed by a Q&A with director Ntare Guma Mbaho Mwine, moderated by Delphine Fawundu

movies.title: Migration And Movement
movies.description: Two sensitive and speculative films chart the migratory experiences of people in the Cuban diaspora. Cuban Roots/Bronx Stories (2000) Dir. Pam Sporn 57min, digital A Black Cuban family in the Bronx experiences some of the great historical events of the 20th century intimately, yet from a distance—Castro’s arrival in Havana, the Bay of Pigs invasion, the Vietnam war—in this singular project by director Pam Sporn. Naufragio (2012) Dir. Dami Sainz Edwards 6min, digital Filmmaker Dami Sainz Edwards uses repetition and superimposition to look at the act of diving into water, evoking the migratory movement of the Cuban people. Introduced by Pam Sporn on Monday, Feb 23

movies.title: Miracle Mile
movies.description: Mostly portrayed in tense real-time, De Jarnatt’s apocalyptic thriller follows a young man who overhears a phone call revealing that a nuclear war has started and missiles will hit Los Angeles within 70 minutes. The bleak exploration of the moments before an impending nuclear holocaust is kept in balance by a romantic fatalism, and contains a unique explicit nod to Pynchon: an apocryphal “Cliff’s Notes for Gravity’s Rainbow .”

movies.title: Miroirs No. 3
movies.description: When piano student Laura (Beer) miraculously survives a car crash, she finds herself in the devoted care of a local woman. Her recovery becomes two-fold as she heals physically and attempts to reconnect with the world, finding a strange harmony with her new adoptive family. Acclaimed director Christian Petzold ( Phoenix , Transit ) spins a modern gothic fairytale revolving around the lies we tell ourselves and the strange ways that grief, connection, and humanity bind and sustain us.

movies.title: Misan Harriman: Shoot The People
movies.cast: Misan Harriman
movies.description:
Shoot The People is a documentary capturing photographer and activist Misan Harriman’s journey documenting global protest movements that drive social change. Renowned for his wide-ranging work — including powerful breakthrough images from the 2020 Black Lives Matter protests and capturing the Palestinian liberation movement on film — Harriman also made history as the first Black man to photograph a British Vogue cover.

The film follows Harriman as he highlights the resilience of grassroots activists fighting for equality, civil rights, and social justice, the film showcases the intersectionality of these movements and their collective power. With historical context, interviews with activists, and explorations of digital activism, the documentary reveals how Harriman's lens brings the world's activism to light, inspiring viewers to recognize their own power in shaping a more just society.

movies.title: Mississippi Masala
movies.description: Mississippi Masala (1991) Dir. Mira Nair With Sarita Choudhury, Denzel Washington 118min; DCP Uganda, US Forced to flee Uganda after dictator Idi Amin expels Asians from the country, Mina (Sarita Choudhury) and her Indian family resettle in Mississippi, hoping to rebuild their lives. There she forms a deep connection with Demetrius (Denzel Washington), a Black local. Their relationship sparks tension as both families and their communities struggle with the racial boundaries it crosses. As hostility grows and pressure mounts, Mina and Demetrius must decide whether to remain loyal to their families or follow their love. Preceded by: Weeyagale (2025) Dir. Ainslie Senfuka With Esme Green, Edith Kaggwa, Abiah Ndagire 6min; DCP UK In English and Ganda with English subtitles A magical-realist drama follows a young British-Ugandan girl whose classroom show-and-tell unlocks a dreamlike journey into her heritage.

movies.title: Mix Nyc Presents Barbara Hammer Through The Eyes Of Others
movies.description: Curated by Jac Renée Bruneau The pioneering lesbian experimental filmmaker Barbara Hammer produced more than 80 films between 1968 and 2019; this program showcases an array of works that explore her artistic output, her as a being, and the ripple effects both continue to have. The filmmaker began this process herself while she was alive— Audience offers a playful array of snippets from conversations about her work with attendees of numerous screenings. The program goes on to move through films by filmmakers who were/are in conversation with Hammer—from engaging in her practices to making homages, writing letters, and (upon Hammer’s invitation) even using her footage. Audience (1982) Dir. Barbara Hammer 32min Love, Barbara (2022) Dir. Brydie O’Connor 15min Untitled (Dyketactics Revisited) (2005) Dir. Liz Rosenfeld 13min Carolee, Barbara and Guvnor (2018) Dir. Lynne Sachs 9min A Video Letter to Barbara Hammer (2018) Dir. Joey Carducci 17min A Month of Single Frames (2019) Dir. Lynne Sachs 14min Followed by a Q&A with Brydie O’Connor and Joey Carducci, moderated by Jac Renée Bruneau

movies.title: Mother Mary
movies.description: Long-buried wounds rise to the surface when iconic pop star Mother Mary (Anne Hathaway) reunites with her estranged best friend and former costume designer Sam Anselm (Michaela Coel) on the eve of her comeback performance. Between original songs from Charli XCX, a protagonist loosely-inspired by Taylor Swift, and a cast including Hathaway, Coel, Hunter Schafer, and FKA Twigs, Lowery’s ( The Green Knight ) latest combines striking fashion with daring drama.

movies.title: Mr Arkadin
movies.description: Zipping around postwar Europe in a mystery that reveals the criminal capitalism that rose in the wake of fascism, this Orson Welles masterpiece (loved by the Cahiers du Cinéma critics) screens on 35mm in the so-called “Corinth” version, AKA Confidential Report —one of nine jumbled variations released over the years. A Pynchonian look at the liminal spaces of Italy, Spain, and Germany after WWII, it features a cast of eccentric character actors like Akim Tamiroff, Paola Mori, Michael Redgrave, and the always magnetic Welles himself.

movies.title: Mubi Notebook Presents: I Am Love
movies.description: The new issue of Notebook , MUBI’s film journal, is devoted to the art of food on film. To celebrate, BAM is thrilled to screen Luca Guadagnino’s lush melodrama I Am Love , featuring an introduction by bestselling cookbook author Alison Roman and critic Elissa Suh. In turn-of-the-millennium Milan, the wife of a wealthy industrialist (Tilda Swinton) slips into a torrid affair with a talented chef (Edoardo Gabbriellini). For these lovers, food and sensuality are one and the same. From cakes to ukha, every dish he prepares only turns up the heat between them—and an unforgettable dish of glazed prawns is their gateway to unbridled passion.

movies.cast:
Kenneth Branagh, 
Michael Keaton, 
Robert Sean Leonard, 
Keanu Reeves, 
Emma Thompson, 
Denzel Washington, 
Kate Beckinsale

movies.title: Mulholland Drive
movies.cast: Justin Theroux, Naomi Watts, Laura Harring
movies.description: Beautiful, bizarre and strangely addictive, the film begins as a botched hit which results in the meeting of brunette amnesiac Rita (Laura Harring – Love in the Time of Cholera) and blonde would-be Hollywood actress Betty (Naomi Watts – Birdman, 21 Grams). Taking the viewer on a memorable neo-noir trip through Hollywood’s dark underbelly, Lynch dispenses with a conventional narrative in favour of a hallucinogenic assault on the senses that will stay with you long after the credits roll. Recently voted the best film of the 21st Century in a BBC Culture poll, MULHOLLAND DRIVE is essential viewing by one of the masters of contemporary American cinema. David Lynch’s scary and seductive vision of Hollywood is a true masterpiece, weaving together a tale of love, jealousy, and revenge like no other.

movies.title: Muppet Treasure Island
movies.cast: Tim Curry, Billy Connolly, Jennifer Saunders, Kevin Bishop, Steve Whitmire, Jerry Nelson, Frank Oz

movies.title: Murmur Of Youth
movies.description: After dropping out of college and discovering the boy she likes doesn’t like her back, suburban Chen takes a job at a Taipei movie theater, where she meets Ling working in the ticket booth. Soon, a slow-simmering friendship grows between them in this sincere and irresistible Taiwanese coming-of-age film directed by Lin Cheng-sheng.

movies.title: My Dinner with André
movies.description: “I treated myself to a taxi. I rode home through the city streets. There wasn’t a street, there wasn’t a building that wasn’t connected to some memory in my mind.” Wallace Shawn and Andre Gregory, playing fictionalized versions of themselves,…

movies.title: My Father’S Shadow
movies.description: My Father’s Shadow (2025) Dir. Akinola Davies Jr. With Sopé Dìrísù 93min; DCP Nigeria, UK In English, Nigerian Pidgin, and Yoruba with English subtitles The UK’s Best International Feature Film entry to the 98th Academy Awards and recipient of the Caméra d’Or Special Mention at Cannes, Akinola Davis Jr.’s My Father’s Shadow is a poetic, tender portrait of father–son bonds. Framed by the political landscape of 1993 Lagos, the film follows a father and his two young sons as they journey into and around the vibrantly rendered Nigerian metropolis, quietly reckoning with their relationship while navigating a city on the precipice of democratic crisis. Brothers and collaborators Akinola Davies Jr. and Wale Davies bring us a groundbreaking feature debut—centering an award-winning performance by Sopé Dìrísù ( Slow Horses , Gangs of London )—that reveals the profound depths of what families leave unspoken. Followed by a Q&A with actor Sopé Dìrísù Preceded by: Lizard (2020) Dir. Akinola Davies Jr. With Pamilerin Ayodeji, Osayi Uzamere, Charles Etubiebi 18min; DCP UK, Nigeria, 18m In English and Pidgin with English subtitles After eight-year-old Juwon gets removed from bible class by her Sunday school teacher, she follows an agama lizard into the bowels of the “Heaven’s Gate Ministries” mega church. Her journey into the labyrinth exposes the financial inner workings and the hidden activities behind the scenes. Plunging her deeper until she is confronted by a spellbinding sermon and a congregation worshipping in a hypnotised frenzy. Magical interactions with an alarmingly larger lizard and a sturdy gateman serve as metaphors for the preceding incidents. As her family proceeds to leave the church, they are intercepted by the dramatic confrontation with a gang of holy armed robbers.

movies.title: My Heart Is That Eternal Rose
movies.description: Tam, perhaps the Hong Kong New Wave’s most daring cine-modernist and a crucial influence on Wong Kar-wai, teams with DP Christopher Doyle for a high-style “heroic bloodshed” melodrama starring Tony Leung Chiu-Wai, Kenny Bee, and Joey Wong as three…

movies.title: My Imaginary Country + Chile’S Student Uprising
movies.description: Chile’s Student Uprising (2014) Dir. Roberto Navarrete 35min; Digital In English and Spanish with English subtitles During the nation’s mass student protests between 2011 and 2013, director Roberto Navarrete traveled to Chile to speak to student leaders like Camila Vallejo and Giorgio Jackson (both later key figures in the Gabriel Boric government) about their demands for a state-funded education system and other radical social changes. In a series of interviews, Chile’s Student Uprising unpacks why these protests had such an effect in Chile and inspired others in the country and beyond. My Imaginary Country (2022) Dir. Patricio Guzmán 83min; DCP In Spanish with English subtitles When the Social Outburst exploded in Chile in 2019, one and a half million people took to the streets of Santiago demanding justice, education, health care, and a new constitution to replace the strident rules imposed on the country during the Pinochet military dictatorship. Patricio Guzmán, a longtime documentarian of Chile’s socio-political landscape, set out to document the demonstrations that would forever alter the trajectory of his nation. Urgent and inspired, My Imaginary Country features harrowing front-line protest footage and interviews with dynamic activist leaders, powerfully connecting Chile's complex, bloody history to contemporary revolutionary social movements—and the election of a new president.

movies.title: My Night at Maud's
movies.description: Rohmer’s first feature-length entry in his “Six Moral Tales” series (following The Bakery Girl of Monceau and Suzanne’s Career) stars Jean-Louis Trintignant as a conscientious Catholic bachelor who is sorely tempted when he meets charming…

movies.title: Mysterious Object At Noon
movies.description: Apichatpong Weerasethakul brought an appetite for experimen­tation to Thai cinema with his debut feature, an uncategorizable work that refracts documentary impressions of his homeland through the surrealist concept of the “exquisite corpse.” Enlisting locals to contribute improvised narration to a simple tale, Weerasethakul charts the collective construction of the fiction as each new encounter imbues it with unpredictable shades of fantasy and pathos. Shot over the course of two years in black-and-white 16mm, Mysterious Object at Noon established the director’s defining fascination with the porous boundaries between the real and the imagined.

movies.title: Nadie Es Inocente (Nobody Is Innocent)
movies.description: This hybrid documentary follows “Kara,” a member of Los Mierdas Punks (The Punk Shits), as he embarks on a train journey to leave behind his life of hell-raising in Ciudad Neza. On his trip, he reflects on the scenes and stories that comprised his debaucherous life. Minter’s pivotal work combines elements of documentary and dramatization, with the young Mierdas Punks playing themselves onscreen and collaborating on the development of the film.

movies.title: Nadja
movies.description: Michael Almereyda’s ( Tesla , Experimenter , Hamlet ) 1994 work of horror—executive produced by David Lynch—centers on young vampire Nadja (Elina Löwensohn) as she attempts to reunite with her twin brother following their father’s death from a stake in the heart at the hands of Dr. Van Helsing (Peter Fonda). The cult-classic, which fuses shimmering black-and-white 35mm with the hallucinatory grain of Pixelvision video, draws inspiration from Dracula’s Daughter (1936) and André Breton’s surrealist novel Nadja . We’re thrilled to screen a brand-new 4K restoration of the director’s cut. A Grasshopper Film and Arbelos Films Release Featuring two Q&As with director Michael Almereyda, moderated on February 6 by critic Stephanie Zacharek at 7pm and on February 7 by filmmaker Azazel Jacobs at 7pm

movies.title: Ndar, Saga Waalo
movies.description: Ndar—the original name of the Senegalese capital Saint-Louis—lies on an island at the mouth of the Senegal River in the former Waalo kingdom, and served as a key port of colonial expansion into West Africa four centuries ago. As an economic, cultural, and political crossroads, the city became a laboratory for France’s so-called “civilizing mission,” where commerce, urban planning, education, and racial mixing were used to assimilate local populations and consolidate colonial power. Today, Saint-Louis holds a complex legacy: while some residents acknowledge this history and maintain longstanding Saint-Louisian traditions, others call for a decisive break from its colonial past. For many young people in particular, the moment demands a new way of thinking about history.

movies.title: NicoláS GuilléN LandriáN Shorts Program
movies.director: Nicolás Guillén Landrián This program of five short films offers an introduction to the subversive Cuban experimental filmmaker and painter Nicolás Guillén Landrián. En un bario Viejo
movies.description: This program of five short films offers an introduction to the subversive Cuban experimental filmmaker and painter Nicolás Guillén Landrián. En un bario Viejo (1963) 9min, digital Life in one of Havana's old neighborhoods is captured on film Los del baile (1965) 6min, digital People dance to a performance by Pello el Afrokán’s Orchestra in this short video essay. Like P.M. , the government censored Los del baile for presenting an “undesirable” image of Havana nightlife. Ociel del Toa (1965) 17min, digital A poetic rendering of the lives of the people who inhabit the banks of the Toa River in Cuba’s Oriente province. Reportaje (1966) 19min, SD file A group of the Cuban poor convene to discuss politics and eventually set a large rag-doll ablaze in an act of collective exorcism. Coffea Arábiga (1968) 18min, digital Commissioned by the government to produce a propaganda film on Cuban coffee, Landrián smuggled dissent into the project, turning it into a cinematic Trojan horse which drew a ban after the so-called Cuban “coffee plan” fell apart. Taller de Linea y 18 (1971) 15min, SD file Landrián’s first project to feature conventional documentary-style narration offers audiences a glimpse inside the workings of a bustling Havana factory.

movies.title: Nighthawks
movies.description: Sergeant DaSilva (Stallone) has to track down and neutralize two terrorist threats in this tense neo-noir. Malmuth’s solo directorial debut, the project was plagued by production problems, with Stallone himself stepping in to help direct and re-edit aspects of the dark cat-and-mouse game. Despite being used as a shooting location for the 57th and 42nd Street stations within the film, a pesky Hoyt-Schermerhorn sign made its way into the film’s final cut.

movies.title: No Other Choice
movies.description: South Korea’s Academy Awards submission for Best Foreign Film is being hailed by critics as an utter masterpiece and earned a rapturous nine-minute standing ovation at this year’s Venice Film Festival. No Other Choice follows one man’s berserk search for a new job after he is abruptly laid off from the paper company where he worked for 25 years. The visionary Park Chan-wook ( Oldboy , Decision to Leave ) helms this captivating black-comedy thriller—one of the most highly anticipated and acclaimed films of the season—adapted from Donald E. Westlake’s 1997 novel The Ax .

movies.title: No Picnic
movies.cast: David Brisbin, Clare Bauman, Judith Malina, Ryan Cutrona, Anne D
movies.description: “ A forgotten eighties NYC movie is back, scuzzier and better than ever. No Picnic captures New York's boho hipster Lower East Side on the edge of Reagan-era gentrification — and a new restoration just saved it from obscurity. ” – David Fear, Rolling Stone

movies.title: Obsession
movies.description: After breaking the mysterious “One Wish Willow” to win his crush’s heart, a hopeless romantic finds himself getting exactly what he asked for. He soon discovers that desire comes at a dark, sinister price in this equally haunting and amusing supernatural horror.
